title: Dispose() causes memory leaks & GodotObject suppresses the Garbage Collector
body:
### Tested versions

Godot 4.4.1

### System information

Godot 4.4.1, Mobile Renderer, Microsoft Windows 11 Pro

### Issue description

I feel like these two "odd ones" will be resolved with one code change, so they belong together.

Please review the code example on this page: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.idisposable?view=net-9.0

>"By implementing IDisposable, you are announcing that instances of this type allocate scarce resources."

Memory is the scarce resource being allocated, so that's what should be cleaned up. Calling `Dispose()` should do the same thing as calling `Free()`.

>"Call the appropriate methods to clean up unmanaged resources here. If disposing is false, only the following code is executed."

Based on my testing, `Dispose()` only removes the handle to the unmanaged object. This is why memory leaks.

>"Use C# finalizer syntax for finalization code. This finalizer will run only if the Dispose method does not get called."

The finalizer is like a "last chance reprisal" if you forget to call `Dispose()`, so it can release any scarce resources. In other words, I should be able to make a custom `GodotObject` that makes the dotnet GC do all the work, like this:

```csharp
public partial class RefManaged : GodotObject
{
    protected override void Dispose(bool disposing)
    {
        // automatically release engine resources when the GC picks 
        // up the managed one. this is what Dispose is intended for.
        // you don't need a separate ref counter on the engine side.
        Free();
        
        base.Dispose(disposing);
    }
}
```

This would work just fine. However, the way `GodotObject` is initialized in the engine prevents the finalizer from being called. At least, I haven't been able to get it to work. It looks like the unmanaged constructor, [ConstructAndInitialize](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/master/modules/mono/glue/GodotSharp/GodotSharp/Core/GodotObject.base.cs), might be stashing a reference that prevents the garbage collector from doing its job.

This is a bug because it violates the dotnet standard for managing scarce external resources (like memory) using `IDisposable`.

### Steps to reproduce

Allocate a bunch of `GodotObject` instances and try calling `Dispose()` instead of `Free()`. Check `IsInstanceValid()` from code, and compare it to the unmanaged objects still allocated in Godot's debugger.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

I provide a [code example here](https://forum.godotengine.org/t/godotobject-vs-refcounted-useless-in-c/109662/11) near the end of the thread. The gentleman on the forum kindly explained that `Dispose()` only releases the managed handle to the unmanaged resource, it doesn't `Free()` the resource itself. That's like if you asked a robot to take out the trash, so it takes the handle off the trash bag and throws it out the window, then lies about the chore being done by saying `IsInstanceValid() == false` while you can see the trash is still there on the floor.
